sections.title: Terrain art checklist

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: WebGL2 terrain reconstructs the compact height field with a Catmull-Rom patch and analytic derivatives; the Canvas2D fallback uses high-quality smoothing instead of nearest-neighbour scaling.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-webgl.js` `sampleBicubic` / `drawBakedGround`; terrain seam tests; visual reference at all four zoom levels.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: A deterministic 2048 × 1024 atlas contains four seamless 256 px variants for grass, forest, rock, sand, snow, earth and wetland. The shader uses relief, macro contrast and fine-crust channels. The sand material receives both the close-view coastal fringe and the previously unused arid weight.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-atlas.js`; five atlas tests; shader-path contract; visual reference. The atlas is procedural by design rather than a downloaded bitmap pack.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Domain-warped elevation, moisture and temperature fields drive normalized material weights. Water uses a smoothed signed-distance field, and a noise-broken sand fringe covers low shores at close zoom. The shore-distance unit now follows each world's resolution instead of a hard-coded four samples per tile.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-webgl.js` material weights, `buildWaterDistance`; three shore-distance regression tests; visual reference.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Atlas painters use periodic noise and seamless tilers; the shader cross-fades variants; height/moisture reconstruction is smooth rather than tile-quantized.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-atlas.test.js` checks every channel and seam; `terrainSeamSpikes` in `terrain-depth.test.js`; visual review.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Four contiguous atlas variants per material are selected by a slow region noise and cross-faded in a ring, including the wrap between variant 3 and 0.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Each material has its own painter, scale and channel response: grass clumps/blades, forest canopy/litter, rock strata/cracks, sand ripples/grit, snow drifts/sparkle, earth clods/grain, wetland pools/reeds.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-atlas.js` painters; per-channel variance tests; visual reference.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Directional sun shading, soft cast-height shadows, baked ambient occlusion, seasonal sun elevation and close-view water-crest highlights. Trees and buildings carry their own grounded shadows on the overlay.
points.docEvidence: `sunState`, `uAO`, shader shadow march and crest path; `terrain-ao.test.js`; `terrain-shader-contract.test.js`; visual reference. Full screen-space shadows for every prop are not claimed.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Hillshade, ambient occlusion, normal/diffuse lighting and slope hachures at map zoom make the smoothed height field legible. Shore stairs are explicitly flattened into banks.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: A persistent wear field is stamped by roads and building footprints, builds up while they exist and recovers slowly. Roads, fields and buildings are drawn from the same world data.
points.docEvidence: `terrain-wear.js`; four wear tests; shader wear tint.

points.label: **Implemented**
points.sourceStatus: Continuous season curves drive palette, sun and effects: snow accumulates through late autumn, peaks in winter and melts through early spring; leaf litter and green-up follow their own ramps. Palette colours are anchored mid-season, trees turn and drop per tree and species (oaks hold brown leaves, conifers stay green), and weather is season-gated so summer cannot snow. Five climate profiles shift the same curves: northern snow arrives earlier and melts later, mediterranean and arid winters hold less snow, and per-species snow retention lets conifers keep their load while birches shed it early. Bare crowns use tapered limbs and snow-tipped twigs; conifers use four snow-bearing tiers.
points.docEvidence: `world/season.js`, `terrain-palette.js`, `seasonal-foliage.js`, `weather.js`; season, weather and foliage tests; `season-year.json`; `climate-reference.json`, `climate-live.json`; transition, grove and both climate sheets.
